canonical.title: Claude Code's native guardrails in 2026: what the permission model holds, and where it stops

parent.title: Running Claude Code safely on a Linux workstation, and where Proxmox actually helps

siblings.title: Threat model and blast radius: what actually goes wrong running an agentic coding CLI on your workstation
siblings.summary: The realized 2026 losses come from the agent's own destructive git commands and from supply-chain malware that weaponizes an installed agent CLI — not from the exotic prompt-injection scenarios; containment must stop out-of-workspace writes, egress, and credential reads, in that order.

siblings.title: Linux-native sandboxing for Claude Code on the workstation itself
siblings.summary: Turn on Claude Code's built-in bubblewrap sandbox, then wrap the whole process in a 30-line bwrap script; systemd-run --user, firejail and Flatpak are the wrong tools for this job, and Landlock is the primitive to bet on but not to hand-roll.

siblings.title: Containers as the containment layer for `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions`
siblings.summary: Rootless Podman plus a proxy-only internal network beats Anthropic's reference devcontainer; the reference firewall leaks DNS and hands the agent NET_ADMIN.

siblings.title: Proxmox as the isolation boundary for Claude Code: KVM VM, not LXC
siblings.summary: Use a KVM VM, never an LXC: Proxmox's own docs say containers share the host kernel and LXC upstream says privileged containers cannot be root-safe — plus the wiring, firewall rules, snapshot policy and sizing to make a dedicated agent guest actually usable.

siblings.title: Credential isolation for an agentic coding CLI on Linux
siblings.summary: An agent that can read $HOME holds your whole identity, and on Linux the keyring does not help — so give the agent its own short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials instead.

siblings.title: Audit trail and recovery drills for an agentic coding CLI on Linux
siblings.summary: Git commits are your real undo and a PostToolUse hook is your real audit log — Claude Code's own transcripts and /rewind are convenience layers that expire, miss bash, and are writable by the agent.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Permission modes
sources.claim: The six permission modes (default/manual, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions), how to set each, protected paths, and exactly what bypassPermissions does and does not skip.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Permissions
sources.claim: Rule evaluation order (deny then ask then allow), settings precedence, per-tool matcher syntax, wrapper stripping, read-only command set, gitignore path anchors, symlink pair checking, and the explicit statement that rules are enforced by Claude Code and not the model.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Sandboxing
sources.claim: The sandboxed Bash tool: bubblewrap + socat + optional seccomp on Linux, Ubuntu 24.04 AppArmor userns fix, default read-everything policy, network proxy allowlist, sandbox settings keys, the dangerouslyDisableSandbox escape hatch, and the documented security limitations including domain fronting and Unix-socket escalation.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Sandbox environments
sources.claim: Comparison of isolation approaches and the instruction that --dangerously-skip-permissions sessions must always run inside a container, VM, or the sandbox runtime.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Security
sources.claim: Built-in protections, additional safeguards (workspace trust, command injection detection, fail-closed matching), the home-directory trust caveat, and the MCP non-audit statement.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Hooks reference
sources.claim: Full hook event list, matcher grammar, handler types, exit-code semantics per event, PreToolUse JSON decision fields, and disableAllHooks / allowManagedHooksOnly.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Hooks guide
sources.claim: The protected-files PreToolUse example, multi-hook merge order, and the key claim that a PreToolUse deny survives bypassPermissions and --dangerously-skip-permissions.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Settings
sources.claim: Settings file locations including /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json on Linux with a managed-settings.d drop-in directory, and the five-level precedence order with managed settings above CLI arguments.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — CLI reference
sources.claim: Flags: --permission-mode values, --dangerously-skip-permissions equivalence, --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions, --allowedTools/--disallowedTools semantics.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — MCP
sources.claim: MCP server trust flow for project-scoped .mcp.json, the rule that a cloned repository cannot approve its own servers, the requiresUserInteraction annotation, and headersHelper executing arbitrary shell commands.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Dev container
sources.claim: Dev container guidance and the warning that a dev container with --dangerously-skip-permissions does not stop exfiltration of ~/.claude credentials.

sources.title: Claude Agent SDK docs — Secure deployment
sources.claim: Anthropic's own framing of the Bash command parser as a permission gate rather than a sandbox, the isolation-strength comparison table, and the credential-injecting proxy pattern.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Auto mode configuration
sources.claim: autoMode schema (environment, allow, soft_deny, hard_deny, $defaults, classifyAllShell), the Recently denied tab, and the warning that conversational boundaries are lost to compaction.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Tools reference
sources.claim: Canonical tool names, which tools require permission in default mode, and the shared rule formats mapping Read rules onto Grep/Glob/LSP and Edit rules onto Write/NotebookEdit.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Authentication
sources.claim: On Linux, Claude Code credentials live in ~/.claude/.credentials.json with file mode 0600 rather than an OS keychain.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Environment variables
sources.claim: IS_SANDBOX is documented as a variable Claude Code sets in subprocesses when running in a sandboxed environment.

sources.title: Claude Code docs — Server-managed settings
sources.claim: Managed sources do not merge, and Anthropic states managed settings are a client-side control rather than a security boundary.

sources.title: code.claude.com/docs/llms.txt — documentation index
sources.claim: The Claude Code documentation index enumerating the permissions, permission-modes, sandboxing, sandbox-environments, hooks, and managed-MCP pages.

sources.title: containers/bubblewrap
sources.claim: bubblewrap is the unprivileged sandboxing tool Claude Code uses on Linux and WSL2, built on user/IPC/PID/network/UTS namespaces plus seccomp filters.

sources.title: anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime
sources.claim: The standalone sandbox runtime wraps a whole process in the same bubblewrap + seccomp isolation, denies all network and all writes by default.

sources.title: claude-code — examples/settings/settings-bash-sandbox.json
sources.claim: Anthropic's own example sandbox settings file, giving the exact key names for autoAllowBashIfSandboxed, allowUnsandboxedCommands, excludedCommands and the network block.

sources.title: claude-code — examples/settings
sources.claim: Anthropic publishes starter settings configurations for common deployment scenarios, including sandbox-specific examples.

sources.title: claude-code — .devcontainer/init-firewall.sh
sources.claim: The reference dev container ships an init-firewall.sh that blocks all outbound traffic except an allowlist, requiring NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW capabilities.

sources.title: Anthropic Engineering — Claude Code sandboxing
sources.claim: Anthropic's engineering rationale for the sandbox: approval fatigue, the two-layer filesystem plus network design, and the assertion that both layers are required.

sources.title: Ona — How Claude Code escapes its own denylist and sandbox
sources.claim: Demonstrated denylist escape via /proc/self/root path identity, the agent choosing to disable its own bubblewrap sandbox, and a hash-blocklist bypass by invoking the dynamic linker directly.

sources.title: Hacker News — discussion of Claude Code sandboxing defaults
sources.claim: Practitioner criticism of the sandbox being opt-in with full default read access and of the agent's ability to disable its own sandbox.

sources.title: GHSA-4q92-rfm6-2cqx — CVE-2026-25724
sources.claim: Deny rules in settings.json were not enforced when files were accessed through symbolic links; CVSS 2.3, CWE-61 and CWE-285, fixed in 2.1.7.

sources.title: GHSA-vp62-r36r-9xqp — CVE-2026-39861
sources.claim: Sandbox escape via symlink following allowed arbitrary file write outside the workspace; High, CVSS 7.7, CWE-22 and CWE-61, fixed in 2.1.64.

sources.title: Hacker News — discussion of CVE-2026-39861
sources.claim: Discussion noting Anthropic's VDP previously excluded symlink-based permission-prompt bypasses from scope, and practitioner scepticism about sandbox strength.

sources.title: oddguan.com — Second time, same sandbox: network allowlist bypass
sources.claim: SOCKS5 hostname null-byte injection bypassed the sandbox network allowlist in every release from 2.0.24 through 2.1.89; fixed in 2.1.90 with no advisory.

sources.title: SecurityWeek — Anthropic silently patches Claude Code sandbox bypass
sources.claim: Press confirmation of the silently patched SOCKS5 allowlist bypass and that Anthropic assigned no CVE and made no public announcement.

sources.title: Adversa AI — Claude Code security bypass: deny rules disabled
sources.claim: Deny rules were silently skipped for shell commands containing more than 50 subcommands, traced to a performance cap.

sources.title: claude-code issue #31558 — deny bypass via env-variable prefix
sources.claim: Reported bypass of deny permissions via an environment-variable command prefix in v2.1.70, since closed.

sources.title: claude-code issue #25000 — sub-agents bypass deny rules
sources.claim: Sub-agents spawned via the Task tool ran 22+ bash commands, including reads of ~/.ssh and ~/.bash_history, despite Bash being in the deny list.

sources.title: claude-code issue #61148 — @../ attachment traversal
sources.claim: A Read deny rule was bypassed by the @../ attachment syntax for files outside the workspace root in v2.1.146; closed as not planned.

sources.title: claude-code issue #24846 — Read deny not enforced for .env
sources.claim: User report that Read deny rules in ~/.claude/settings.json were not enforced for .env files.

sources.title: claude-code issue #26315 — Windows-path deny rules never match
sources.claim: Deny rules written with Windows-style backslash paths for Write/Edit on .claude/*.json did not match, illustrating the path-anchor footgun.

sources.title: Hacker News — IS_SANDBOX=1 with --dangerously-skip-permissions
sources.claim: Practitioners pass IS_SANDBOX=1 alongside claude --dangerously-skip-permissions, with discussion of prefix versus export semantics.

sources.title: Claude Code Camp — how the sandbox works and what it doesn't protect
sources.claim: Hands-on testing showing sandbox.denyRead does not stop Claude's Read tool, and the binary's embedded unsandboxed-retry instruction.
